summary.text: A four-year-old girl was admitted with left upper limb pain after falling from a step; X-ray showed no fractures or other serious abnormalities, the pain persisted the next day and her arm was splinted in pronation before referral.

Left elbow ultrasonography showed the annular ligament and supinator muscle entrapped in the radiohumeral joint with an enlarged joint space; the right elbow showed no inclusions or supinator swelling; the elbow could not be reduced by pronation and supination maneuvers.

She was supervised without elbow immobilization for one week, after which elbow pain spontaneously improved without limitation in range of motion; ultrasonography showed no entrapment but persistent supinator thickening, and the authors report spontaneous reduction.

summary.text: A three-year-old girl had left upper limb pain and stopped moving the limb after her mother pulled her left hand; X-ray of the left elbow at a nearby clinic found no obvious abnormalities, she was diagnosed with pulled elbow, and manipulation gave no improvement.
Symptoms did not improve the next day and she was referred two days after the injury with her left arm in a splint; her left forearm was pronated and she did not move it due to pain.

Left elbow ultrasonography showed an entrapped, swollen supinator with an enlarged joint space, confirming pulled elbow; the right elbow showed no inclusions or swelling; pronation and supination maneuvers did not reduce it.

She was managed with supervised neglect without immobilization; four days later pain and range of motion improved and ultrasonography showed no entrapment with persistent supinator swelling, which significantly improved one week later.
